summary: In Greek mythology, Clytius (Ancient Greek Κλυτίος) of Oechalia is an Argonaut — son of King Eurytus and Antiope (or Antioche), brother of Iole, Iphitos, and other Eurytids. Hyginus has him killed by Aeetes; Diodorus instead has Heracles kill him in the war on Eurytus.

sections.heading: Eurytid Argonaut
paragraphs: Apollonius (Argonautica 1.86) and Hyginus (Fabulae 14) list Clytius son of Eurytus among the Argo's crew; Apollodorus (Bibliotheca 1.9.16) likewise. Hyginus has Aeetes kill him at Colchis (if the text is sound); Diodorus (4.37.5) places his death in Heracles' war against Eurytus.
Wikipedia's crowded Clytius page also covers the Giant slain by Hecate, Laomedon's Trojan son (clytius-trojan), Penelope's suitors, Dolops' Achaean father, and many others.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id clytius-oechalia is the Oechalian Argonaut alone — not clytius-giant, clytius-trojan, clytius-achaean, or the suitor stubs clytius-same / clytius-zacynthus.
